visualReview.notes: Actually inspected 86 final images: 15 portable, 15 shared, 31 medium-fi and 25 normal terrain views. Compared actual museum western, snowy courtyard, east/night and northern bridge photographs. Five distinct towers, pale northwest/southeast uppers, brick southwest/northeast/gate towers, open courtyard, north/east palace wings, covered curtain walks, south balcony, eyebrow dormers and four bridge arches remain recognizable. Original roofs and relative facade proportions remain photograph-guided. Replaced the rectangular provisional contact plinth with the assembled occupied boundary and buried feet; extended bridge piers to retained ground. Added mapped northern path and concrete steps plus narrow western gate connector. Initial steep civil support walls were revised to sloped earth supports before these final images. Exact embankment profile, facade niches, stone patches, window counts and dormer shapes are approximate.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Seven canonical graphs: granite, brick, lime plaster, plain timber, ceramic tile, painted metal and rammed earth. Carved ornament shares tinted plaster and sandstone parts share tinted granite; opaque glass and recesses share one local PBR slot. Skyline bakes common linear material means into one draw. Six GLBs contain zero images. Actual shared renders show consistent masonry, pale facades and tile roofs; each graph is read once and unload releases model geometry. No photograph pixels were copied. The shared fixture uses flat terrain, which partly buries foundations and earth connectors; true contact is independently captured against retained terrain.

mediumFiReview.notes: All 31 final medium-fi images actually inspected: noon/late, economy/high, ten architecture cameras, four whole-castle browser levels and transitions. Skyline keeps five towers, open court, western passage, north bridge arches and civil connections at 898 triangles. District adds blind-niche and facade cards at 3709 triangles. Street retains recessed openings, chimneys, dormers, northern step treads/rails and principal ornament at 13581 triangles. Close-up adds tile relief, mullions, trim, fieldstone patches and south balcony details at 41975 triangles. Small decoration and treads fade at far levels. Whole-castle composition and material means remain consistent; synthetic neighboring buildings do not prove the real park or town.

geographicReview.notes: Fresh relation 1579104 v31 identifies exact Q209643. Retained component coordinates agree within 0.683 mm. Native +X points east-southeast at 102.866 degrees and +Z south-southwest at 192.866 degrees. Western gate, paired pale/brick corner towers, north/east palace and north bridge sign heading -0.224560956675 rad at [26.472922093,53.451203802]. Fresh mapped bridge polygon, connected steps way429889553 and northern path way429889566 are retained separately. No mirror or rescaling. One public Terrarium numeric tile generates 4225 native samples at 4 m spacing over 256 m. Y0 is decoded 175.0822 m anchor working datum, not a surveyed regional or ellipsoidal datum. One rigid +0.375 m translation gives court floor from highest occupied sample plus 0.25 m. Exterior feet and bridge piers extend four meters below retained grade; mapped narrow civil connections end at grade. Coarse data does not resolve actual embankment/forecourt surfaces. No whole-precinct cutout or park replacement.

fidelityReview.notes: Accepted medium-fi reconstruction of the five-tower castle, open court, palace, wall walks, northern bridge and narrow mapped civil connections. Original 255892-triangle, 24453976-byte master is independently reproducible at sha256:f309ea5ba68616121c06e1529e32274ebbabb6ae386a14da3e273f40bb32ecee from unchanged mir-castle-model.mjs#mirStudy.build. Separate chapel-crypt, watchman house, palace annex/ruins, lake/moat, park/ramparts and memorial of the wider UNESCO complex are outside this source coverage. ICOMOS 2000 describes 22–26 m towers while map roof tags use 30/31 m; roof inclusion/datum remains unresolved, so current body/eave/roof proportions are interpreted rather than surveyed. Coarse terrain may include buildings or vegetation and does not establish DEM resolution, vintage or vertical accuracy. Civil earth slopes, step rise/count, western connector, stone patches and facade details remain approximations. Museum gallery upload paths are not photo dates; individual photographers and capture dates are unestablished. No physical-device or universal host-terrain claim.

legacyFidelityScope.notes: Maximum fidelity pending: facade proportions, blind-niche patterns, window counts, roof dormers and ridge/chimney positions are photographic interpretations rather than measured restoration drawings. The castle and northern arched bridge are modeled. The separate chapel-crypt, guardhouse, park, moat, earth ramparts and later palace remains of the wider complex still need authored geometry. Map tower roof heights of 30/31 m differ from the ICOMOS evaluation’s 22–26 m tower dimensions. Height datum and roof inclusion need resolution before geographic completion. Bridge arch count follows the museum view; pier geometry, deck elevation and contact with the approach embankment remain provisional. A narrow castle contact plinth is not a surveyed terrain model. Eight reusable procedural material graphs provide brick, lime plaster, granite, raw limestone, sandstone, timber, ceramic tile and painted metal. Glass is local PBR color; no embedded photographs.
legacyFidelityScope.reviewBinding: Historical record only; current approval is the newly inspected medium-fi scope.

geometryValidation.notes: Three focused tests pass: original master bytes independently reproduce; current source/runtime hashes and retained input hashes agree; exact signed map frame is accepted. All four browser levels keep the roofless court, traversable gate and four bridge barrels. Front-face rays test the assembled exterior boundary, not internal tower/palace seams, and find feet at sampled grade. Child-process LOD builds reproduce exact bytes within 1000/4000/16000/64000 triangles, eight draws and 3 MB initial download. Separate POSITION/NORMAL 12-byte streams prevent duplicated upload layout. Six GLBs pass Khronos with zero errors, warnings and images; strict medium-fi has no findings. Normal-placement origin offset is zero within 0.1 mm, ground rays differ from independently reconstructed triangular ground by 0.0151 m or less, bridge passages pass at all five levels, and five unloads leave zero model geometries. These are targeted sampled checks, not an exhaustive manifold or architectural survey.

Skyline plus district: 345764 bytes. Physical laptop/phone measurements remain pending.

limitations: Original 255892-triangle / 24453976-byte master is independently reproducible at sha256:f309ea5ba68616121c06e1529e32274ebbabb6ae386a14da3e273f40bb32ecee from mir-castle-model.mjs#mirStudy.build.

Fresh exact-Q209643 relation 1579104 v31 and retained component polygons agree within 0.683 mm. Native +X east-southeast at 102.866 degrees, +Z south-southwest at 192.866 degrees; west gate, differently colored corner towers, north/east palace wings and north bridge sign heading -0.224560956675. Retained Terrarium numeric terrain forms a 4225-value 4 m native grid. Y0 is decoded 175.0822 m anchor working datum, not surveyed regional/ellipsoidal elevation. Reconstructed court floor 0.375 m above anchor uses highest sample inside occupied rectangle plus 0.25 m. One rigid translation preserves relative facade/roof heights. Occupied mapped feet and bridge piers extend four meters below retained grade. Northern path/steps and narrow west gate connector meet retained ground; approach elevations, embankment widths and vertical survey remain approximate. No whole-precinct terrain replacement or cutout.

Retained coarse terrain does not resolve narrow castle foundations, the northern embankment or paved west forecourt. Numeric source resolution, vertical datum, vintage and under-building contamination are unverified.

Architectural courtyard floor uses highest sample inside the mapped occupied rectangle plus 0.25 m; one rigid translation preserves relative building proportions. Buried mapped feet and four bridge piers meet this product.

The narrow northern path/steps and west gate connector are reconstructed civil surfaces tied to mapped lines and retained grade. Their elevations, earth banks and exact width are not a survey; the surrounding park, moat and ramparts remain host terrain.

ICOMOS 2000 tower heights 22–26 m and mapped roof heights 30/31 m have unresolved roof/datum scope. Body/eave heights of the interpretation and photographed proportions remain explicit rather than presented as measured restoration values.

Accepted exterior scope is the five-tower castle, open courtyard, L-shaped palace, wall walks, north four-arched bridge and mapped civil connectors. Chapel-crypt, watchman house, palace annex/ruins, park, lake/moat, earth ramparts and massacre memorial of the wider UNESCO complex are separate structures not supplied here.

Seven canonical graphs provide granite, brick, plaster, timber, ceramic tile, painted metal and rammed earth. Carved and sandstone details share existing slots with component tints. Opaque PBR glass/recess uses no image. Skyline bakes the common linear means. Fine fieldstone placement, facade niches, window/dormer counts and roof curves remain approximations.

Northern embankment and west forecourt are not resolved by coarse terrain. Narrow mapped civil connections include bounded interpreted earth support, not a measured landscape replacement. Physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured.

terrainReview.notes: Actually inspected all 25 final normal-placement images, five cameras for source plus four browser levels. Signed heading and explicit retained terrain reference give zero model-origin offset within 0.1 mm. Three open-ground probes match independent triangular interpolation with a 0.015 m fixture offset. Sampled assembled exterior front faces meet terrain and all four arch passages remain open. Five unloads restore ground and release model geometry. Narrow civil connectors and their earth supports are reconstructed to this coarse product; actual site levels and embankments remain unverified. Numeric terrain inputs are not model textures; OSM/terrain attribution remains explicit.
